title: Castle Waldeck
teaser: Count Waldeck invited his guests to a night of vampires, and the blizzard raised the drawbridge behind them. In the morning the Count was found in his bedchamber with two dark punctures on his neck and a string of garlic on his chest, as if someone had first killed a vampire and then decided to stop him for good. Every guest wore a high-collared cloak, and that night practically the only person not roaming the castle corridors was the Count himself.

habits.label: Wax fangs
habits.habit: Wax fangs in their waistcoat pocket
clues: In the chapel a squashed wax fang with tooth marks lies on the lid of the prop coffin. The culprit carries wax fangs.
Under a chair by the fireplace in the banqueting hall someone found a pair of wax fangs, still soft from the warmth of a hand. The culprit has wax fangs.

habits.label: Scarlet lining
habits.habit: A cloak lined with scarlet silk
clues: A scarlet silk thread, the silk used for cloak linings, hangs on a bracket by the wine cellar door. The culprit has a cloak with a scarlet lining.
A footman saw a black cloak swing open on the spiral stairs of the north tower and a flash of red lining. The culprit has a cloak with a scarlet lining.

habits.label: Aspen stake
habits.habit: An aspen stake tucked in their belt
clues: There are fresh aspen shavings on the library carpet, as if a stake was sharpened right by the fireplace. The culprit carries an aspen stake in their belt.
An aspen stake with a scrap of belt strap is stuck in a crack between the stones of the north tower. The culprit carries an aspen stake in their belt.

habits.label: Silver crucifix
habits.habit: A silver crucifix worn over their costume
clues: The dusty shelf in the wine cellar has the print of a small cross on a chain, as if someone leaned low over the bottles. The culprit wears a silver crucifix round their neck.
An old maid saw someone in the banqueting hall clutch a silver crucifix to their chest at every gust of wind against the windows. The culprit wears a silver crucifix.

habits.label: Bat brooch
habits.habit: A bat-shaped brooch on their collar
clues: In the library a bat-shaped brooch with a bent pin is stuck between the pages of Polidori's The Vampyre. The culprit has a bat brooch.
The velvet bed canopy in the Count's bedchamber has a pinhole and a crumb of black enamel from a wing. The culprit wears a bat-shaped brooch.

habits.label: Whitened face
habits.habit: Face whitened with rice powder like a corpse
clues: The pillow in the Count's bedchamber has a white mark of rice powder, and the Count didn't wear make-up that night. The culprit has a whitened face.
In the stables a post by the stall has a white smear of powder at cheek height. The culprit's face is whitened with powder.

habits.label: Smells of slivovitz
clues: In the wine cellar a bottle of slivovitz has been uncorked, though the Count kept only wine there. The culprit smells of slivovitz.
A flat flask was left on a pew in the chapel, and its neck smells of slivovitz. The culprit reeks of slivovitz.

habits.label: Takes snuff
habits.habit: Takes snuff from a silver snuffbox
clues: A pinch of brown snuff is scattered on the library windowsill. The culprit takes snuff.
The kitchen boy heard a loud sneeze in the dark wine cellar, then the click of a snuffbox lid. The culprit takes snuff from a snuffbox.

habits.label: Limps
clues: In the snow by the stables there's a line of footprints, and the left one is everywhere shallower and smeared. The culprit limps on the left leg.
The old maid remembers a cloaked figure in the banqueting hall walking along the table favouring one leg. The culprit limps.

habits.label: Bone rosary
habits.habit: Tells the beads of a bone rosary
clues: In the chapel three yellow bone beads from a broken string are scattered by the lectern. The culprit carries a bone rosary.
A footman heard a dry clicking in the library, as if someone in the dark were telling bone beads. The culprit tells the beads of a bone rosary.

habits.label: Grey streak
habits.habit: A grey streak above the forehead
clues: The kitchen boy saw a hood at the banqueting hall doors with a white streak escaping from under it. The culprit has a grey streak above the forehead.
In the north tower a long grey hair hangs in a cobweb by the low lintel, with dark ones beside it. The culprit has a grey streak in their hair.

habits.label: Bear claw
habits.habit: A bear claw on a leather cord
clues: A bear claw drilled for a cord was found in the straw in the stables. The culprit wears a bear claw on a cord.
The door frame of the Count's bedchamber has a fresh deep scratch at chest height, as if a claw hanging from someone's neck caught it. The culprit wears a bear claw round their neck.

habits.label: Smells of camphor
clues: In the north tower a sharp smell of camphor cuts through the damp and the smell of mice. The culprit smells of camphor.
The bed curtains in the Count's bedchamber smell of camphor, though the castle linen is stored with lavender. The culprit smells of camphor.

habits.label: Scar on the cheek
habits.habit: A duelling scar right across the cheek
clues: In the library the last line in the Count's diary reads: "Scar on the cheek. Don't believe a single word." The culprit has a duelling scar on their cheek.
By candlelight a maid in the wine cellar made out a face with a thin scar right across the cheek. The culprit has a scar on their cheek.

habits.label: Latin sayings
clues: "Memento mori" is chalked on the chapel wall, and the chalk hasn't flaked yet. The culprit is full of Latin sayings.
The kitchen boy heard "In vino veritas" spoken over a glass in the banqueting hall, followed by a short laugh. The culprit is full of Latin sayings.

habits.label: Lump sugar
habits.habit: Carries lump sugar in their pocket
clues: In the stables, by the stall of the Count's stallion, there are crumbs of lump sugar, and the horses here aren't spoiled with sugar. The culprit carries lump sugar in their pocket.
A lump of sugar with fluff from cloth on it, as if from a pocket, lies by the bed in the Count's bedchamber. The culprit has lump sugar in their pocket.

safe: The iron casket in the library was opened with the combination, and the mortgage on the castle is missing from it. The culprit knows the safe combination.
Behind a tapestry in the Count's bedchamber there's a fireproof safe; its door is pushed to, but the bundle with the will isn't inside. The culprit knows the safe combination.
keys: The Count's bedchamber is locked with two turns of the key at night, and in the morning the door was locked again, with not a scratch on the lock. The culprit had keys.
The wine cellar grille was opened with a key and carefully locked behind. The culprit had keys.
medic: The glass at the head of the bed in the Count's bedchamber has a bitter sediment: the Count fell asleep long before the two punctures appeared on his neck. The culprit knows about poisons.
In the wine cellar, belladonna tincture was mixed into the bottle of Tokaji the Count ordered brought upstairs. The culprit knows about poisons.
cash: A month of the servants' wages is gone from the cash box in the library, yet the ledger balances to the last kreuzer. The culprit had access to money.
Under the Count's plate in the banqueting hall someone found a receipt for three thousand gulden, and the castle hasn't seen that kind of money since spring. The culprit had access to money.
passages: A passage in the thickness of the wall leads from the chapel to the Count's bedchamber. Only the old servants remember it, and the cobwebs in it are torn. The culprit knows the service passages.
The north tower door is locked from outside, but fresh footprints in the dust lead to it from the wine cellar through a forgotten underground corridor. The culprit knows the service passages.
sched: By long custom hot wine is brought to the Count's bedchamber every night at two, yet that night the jug stood by the door ten minutes early. The culprit knows the schedule.

The footman leaves the banqueting hall at half past one to put out the candelabra, and that's exactly when the string of garlic vanished from the wall above the fireplace. The culprit knows the schedule.
quiet: The floorboards by the Count's bedchamber creak so loudly they can be heard through the wall, yet the footman in the next room never woke. The culprit moves silently.
In the north tower the bats take off from the beams at any step, yet that night nobody disturbed them. The culprit moves silently.
strong: The oak lid of the prop coffin in the chapel takes four to lift, yet one person shifted it and put it back. The culprit is physically strong.
The stable doors, frozen to the threshold, were flung open with a single heave, and there's a fresh chip in the ice. The culprit is physically strong.
tools: In the Count's bedchamber the window catch was taken apart and reassembled, not a scratch on the brass. The culprit is handy with tools.
In the stables two nails were pulled from the shoe of the Count's stallion, and now nobody can ride out of the castle. The culprit is handy with tools.
french: A card is pinned to the string of garlic on the Count's chest in the bedchamber: "Dors bien, mon vampire", French for "Sleep well, my vampire". The culprit knows French.
Of all the shelves of books on vampires in the library, only Calmet's French treatise was taken down, and the bookmark lies at the chapter on how to lay a corpse to rest. The culprit knows French.
